## **Why Multivariate Normal Distributions?**

[Explain why controlled distributions are useful.]

## **The Experimental Strategy**

We systematically vary:

- dimensionality,
- variance structure,
- correlation structure,
- anisotropy,
- coordinate representation.

The main quantities of interest are:

- warmup length,
- nested $\widehat{R}$,
- mean squared error.

<style>
.button-container {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 10px;
  margin: 20px 0;
}

.cov-button {
  padding: 10px 20px;
  background-color: #f0f0f0;
  border: 2px solid #ccc;
  border-radius: 5px;
  cursor: pointer;
  font-size: 14px;
  font-weight: 500;
  transition: all 0.3s ease;
}

.cov-button:hover {
  background-color: #e0e0e0;
  border-color: #999;
}

.cov-button.active {
  background-color: #4a90d9;
  color: white;
  border-color: #4a90d9;
}

.plot-container {
  display: none;
  margin-top: 20px;
}

.plot-container img {
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}

.plot-container:first-of-type {
  display: block;
}
</style>

<script>
function showPlot(plotId) {
  const allPlots = document.querySelectorAll('.plot-container');
  allPlots.forEach(plot => plot.style.display = 'none');

  const allButtons = document.querySelectorAll('.cov-button');
  allButtons.forEach(btn => btn.classList.remove('active'));

  const selectedPlot = document.getElementById(plotId);
  if (selectedPlot) {
    selectedPlot.style.display = 'block';
  }

  event.currentTarget.classList.add('active');
}
</script>
